questions.stem: The Jnanpith Award — India's highest literary honour — was instituted in:
questions.explanation: Jnanpith Award — instituted 1965 by Sahu Shanti Prasad Jain (Bharatiya Jnanpith trust). First recipient: G. Sankara Kurup (Malayalam, 1965, for Odakkuzhal). Awarded annually to an Indian writer for outstanding contribution to literature in any of the 22 languages on the Constitution's Eighth Schedule + English. Prize: ₹21 lakh + bronze Saraswati statue + citation. Most-awarded language: Hindi (11 awards). 'Jnanpith' literally = 'seat of knowledge'.

questions.stem: The Sahitya Akademi — India's National Academy of Letters — was set up in:
questions.explanation: Sahitya Akademi — established 12 March 1954 by GoI; registered as a society 1956. Headquartered in Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi. First president — Jawaharlal Nehru. Recognises 24 Indian languages. Awards Sahitya Akademi Awards annually (₹1 lakh + plaque) for best literary work in each. Bal Sahitya Puraskar (children's literature) and Yuva Puraskar (under-35 authors). Bhasha Samman for lesser-known languages. Sister organisations: Lalit Kala Akademi (visual arts), Sangeet Natak Akademi (performing arts).

questions.stem: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature (1913) for which work?

options.option_text: Gitanjali (Song Offerings) — English translation by Tagore himself

questions.explanation: Tagore — first non-European Nobel Literature laureate, 1913. Recognized for Gitanjali (Bengali 1910; English 1912 with intro by W.B. Yeats). 103 prose-poems on devotion. Tagore wrote in Bengali but translated his own work into English. Also wrote two national anthems — Jana Gana Mana (India) and Amar Sonar Bangla (Bangladesh). Knighted 1915, renounced after Jallianwala Bagh 1919. Founded Visva-Bharati at Shantiniketan (UNESCO WHS 2023).

questions.explanation: 'Train to Pakistan' (1956) is by Khushwant Singh, NOT R.K. Narayan. R.K. Narayan wrote 'Swami and Friends', 'The Guide' (Sahitya Akademi 1960), 'The English Teacher' — all set in fictional Malgudi. Rushdie's 'Midnight's Children' (1981) won Booker (1981) + Booker of Bookers (1993, 25th anniversary) + Best of Booker (2008, 40th). Other Booker winners by Indian / Indian-origin authors: Arundhati Roy 'God of Small Things' (1997), Aravind Adiga 'White Tiger' (2008), Geetanjali Shree 'Tomb of Sand' (Hindi, 2022 — first Indian-language).

questions.stem: Which Indian language has the most Jnanpith Award winners as of 2025?
questions.explanation: Hindi — 11 Jnanpith awards (most). Notable Hindi winners: Sumitranandan Pant (1968), Ramdhari Singh Dinkar (1972), S.H. Vatsyayan 'Agyeya' (1978), Mahadevi Verma (1982), Nirmal Verma (1999). Kannada — 8 Jnanpith winners (Karnataka holds the next-highest tally). Bengali — 6, Malayalam — 6, Marathi — 5, Tamil — 3, Telugu — 3 (incl. Viswanatha Satyanarayana 1970). Latest awards (58th + 59th, 2023) — Damodar Mauzo (Konkani) and Rambhadracharya (Sanskrit) jointly with Gulzar (Urdu).

questions.stem: The 'Anand Math' (1882) — the novel that gave India 'Vande Mataram' — was written by:
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee — wrote 'Anandmath' (1882, Bengali). The novel is set during the Sannyasi Rebellion (1770s, Bengal). 'Vande Mataram' first appeared in Anandmath. Adopted as the National Song of India (declared 24 January 1950, alongside Jana Gana Mana as anthem). Sung at INC's 1896 Calcutta session by Tagore himself. First two stanzas widely sung. Bankim's other major novels — Durgeshnandini (1865, first Bengali novel), Kapalkundala, Krishnakanta's Will.

questions.stem: Geetanjali Shree won the 2022 International Booker Prize for 'Tomb of Sand' — making it the FIRST Indian-language work to win. The original language was:
questions.explanation: 'Ret Samadhi' (Hindi, 2018) — by Geetanjali Shree. Translated to English as 'Tomb of Sand' by Daisy Rockwell. Won International Booker Prize 2022 (announced 26 May 2022) — first Indian-language work to do so. Prize £50,000 split equally between author + translator. Story — an 80-year-old widow rebuilds her life, eventually returning to Pakistan (her birthplace) for closure on Partition. Other Indian Booker stories: Arundhati Roy (1997), Adiga (2008), Salman Rushdie (1981, 2008).
